problem: Zero-shot ObjectNav methods over-rely on semantic reasoning even when semantic cues are weak or ambiguous, which hurts exploration efficiency. They also identify targets from single-frame detections or max-confidence fusion, so sporadic high-confidence misdetections cause false-positive stops.
motivation: Humans explore quickly when cues are weak, focus on likely regions when cues are strong, and gather more observations before committing to a target-like object. Efficient and reliable zero-shot ObjectNav needs adaptive use of semantics and robust multi-frame target identification under noisy detectors.
key_idea: Switch adaptively between semantic (TSP-ordered high-score frontiers) and geometry (nearest-frontier) exploration based on the frontier semantic-score distribution, and fuse multi-frame detections of the target and LLM-listed similar objects at object-cluster level with volume-weighted confidence and absence penalties.
insight: Two-stage adaptive exploration beats every single-stage strategy and the utility-based baseline on HM3Dv2 (SR 76.20 vs 72.90-74.50 single-stage, 74.40 utility). Semantic TSP plus geometry greedy works best, and thresholds show a hump shape (best sigma_t=0.015, r_t=1.10). For fusion, removing it drops HM3Dv2 SR to 55.00 and max-fusion gives 67.90. Fusion also permits a lower detector threshold than a higher-DCT variant, which reaches only 68.20 on HM3Dv2.
method: Environmental mapping: 2D probabilistic grid frontier map with PCA-clustered frontiers, plus a VLFM-style BLIP-2 semantic score map with FoV-based cos^2 confidence and a confidence-weighted average update. Prompts are augmented with LLM-inferred room names.

Mode-switching criteria: compute the max-to-mean ratio r and standard deviation sigma of frontier semantic scores. Semantic mode is used only if r>r_t (1.10) and sigma>sigma_t (0.015); otherwise geometry mode is used.

Semantic-based exploration: select high-score frontiers and solve an asymmetric TSP with the LKH solver over A* path-length costs (zero return cost). The first frontier on the tour becomes the goal, avoiding greedy oscillation.
Geometry-based exploration: nearest-frontier greedy selection, which the ablation shows outperforms TSP for ObjectNav.

Target-centric semantic fusion: DeepSeek-V3 (chain-of-thought) offline generates a list of similar/misdetectable objects, an adaptive confidence threshold c_th, and the likely room. YOLOv7 or Grounding-DINO detects, Mobile-SAM segments, and each object cluster keeps per-label point cloud, confidence and volume. Fusion is volume-weighted, absent labels in the FoV are fused with confidence 0 (penalty), and the best label maximizes c*n.

Reliable/suspected target selection: clusters whose best label is the target and whose confidence exceeds c_th are reliable and navigated to. Lower-confidence ones are suspected targets, used only after frontiers run out.

Safe waypoint navigation: A* path, local target beyond 0.75 m, and action selection by the sum of target-distance, proximity-change and ESDF-based safety costs. MINCO trajectories are used on the real robot.

setting.backbone: Frozen foundation models: BLIP-2 (score map), DeepSeek-V3 (offline object/room/threshold reasoning), YOLOv7 / Grounding-DINO + Mobile-SAM (detection/segmentation)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + odometry (displacement and orientation relative to the start)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: move_forward 0.25 m, turn_left/right 30°, look_up/down 30°, stop; continuous MINCO trajectories on the real robot
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3Dv1, HM3Dv2, MP3D) plus real world

numbers.eval_set_note: HM3Dv1 (HM3D-Semantics v0.1, 2022 Habitat Challenge, 2000 episodes, 20 scenes)
numbers.extra: 500 step limit, success distance 0.2 m (stated in the paper's implementation details)

numbers_note: The paper does not state split names; the official Habitat challenge validation sets are assumed, hence 'val'. SPL is printed as 33.0/38.0/17.8 in Table 1, and 32.95/38.03/17.81 in the fusion ablation table. The real-world result (6 trials: SR 100%, SPL 0.723) is not a benchmark and is omitted.
results: ApexNav is best zero-shot on HM3Dv1 (SR 59.6, SPL 33.0) and HM3Dv2 (SR 76.2, SPL 38.0). The main baselines are TriHelper (SR 56.5 on HM3Dv1) and VLFM (SR 63.6, SPL 32.5 on HM3Dv2). On MP3D it has the best SPL (17.8) and SR 39.2, slightly below SG-Nav's 40.2. Real-world tests with an AgileX LIMO robot succeeded in 6/6 trials.
limitations: Uses a single-layer 2D map, so cross-floor targets fail; the 'Different Floor' failure class exceeds 13% on HM3Dv1 and MP3D, with more failures when starting on stairs.
Detector false positives (over 11% of episodes) and dataset annotation gaps cause failures; small/ambiguous objects such as plants are missed.
Assumes visible targets and fully explored sensor view, and semantic guidance fails when the target has weak semantic relevance to its surroundings.
